blocks.text: Less assumption. More understanding.

LensFleet began with a simple observation: a status update is not proof. Delivered, visited, patrolled and on site are updates. We’re building a way to review the locations, times and recordings behind them.

The planned platform brings together six areas: transport and delivery, security, care, pets, creators and assets. Sentinel is the planned business product; LensFleet Home is the planned household experience.
LensFleet is a UK company developing its product for transport, service, security and household needs, including Lagos.
A clearer view of everyday operations.

To give any organisation or household a camera-enabled, location-aware platform that records what happened, where and when, protects that record, and lets it be shared with exactly the people who need to see it — no more, no less.
A world where the record is clear.
A world in which the movement of people, goods and services is transparent, trusted and verifiable, so that the people who depend on it can act on evidence rather than assumption.
Precise technology. A human purpose.
Proof over promise
A clip, a position, a count, a timestamp. Every feature should help you answer what happened.
Transparent, not intrusive
Show what is needed to the people who need it. Sharing is deliberate, time-boxed and revocable.
Plain language
Clear words for the Lagos bus owner and the London care manager. Specific times, places and counts.
One platform, many fronts
One platform for business operations and household needs, with words and defaults that fit your world.
Built for where it will run
Patchy networks, hot cabins, two currencies. Design for Lagos conditions first.

Website privacy notice
This expanded draft describes the development-stage website and identifies the decisions still awaiting approval. It is not an adopted policy or service agreement.
Who this notice concerns

This draft covers general enquiries sent through the LensFleet marketing website. LensFleet Limited, company no. 16970123, is the company contact. Registered office: Flat 2 Milligan House, 99 Avenue Road, London N14 4FH. Product location and camera data need a separate, deployment-specific notice.
What the form collects

The form asks for your name, email address, area of interest and message, plus an optional organisation name. It also sends the request type (general enquiry or Home waitlist) and elapsed form-completion time. Do not send recordings, location histories, medical details or sensitive incident information.
Why the information is used

Enquiries are sent to the team so they can answer questions, discuss future pricing or product plans. A Home waitlist request asks the team to email you about launch availability. The owner must approve and document the lawful basis for each purpose before adopting this notice.
How delivery works

The website server validates the form and uses Resend to send accepted enquiries to the configured team mailbox. The form does not write enquiries to an application database. Delivery-provider acceptance does not establish that a person has read the message.
Security and technical records

The server keeps a temporary in-memory request counter keyed by connection address to limit repeated submissions. Entries expire after ten minutes and are removed on subsequent requests; a server restart also clears them. Hosting and email services may keep separate technical logs. Their locations and retention must be confirmed by the owner.
Retention, recipients and transfers — awaiting approval

The owner must confirm the team mailbox retention period, waitlist deletion process, processor terms, hosting location and any international transfer arrangements. No period or data-residency promise has been approved. This is an outstanding requirement before public launch.
Questions and rights

Email info@lensfleet.com to ask about access, correction, deletion or objections to processing, or to withdraw a Home waitlist request. The rights that apply depend on the processing and jurisdiction. You can also contact the UK Information Commissioner or Nigeria Data Protection Commission. The owner must approve the request-handling procedure before this notice is adopted.
Regulator information: UK Information Commissioner · Nigeria Data Protection Commission.

Body cameras and consent in care
A camera changes the experience of a visit. Discuss the people and the purpose before the device.
Start with the purpose
Define the problem you are trying to solve and whether recording is necessary. Involve the care provider, workers, people receiving care and their representatives in the decision.
Agree the rules before recording

Ask your privacy adviser to assess the lawful basis, transparency, sensitive information, worker monitoring and any impact assessment required in your jurisdiction. Consent alone is not a substitute for that assessment.
Make access deliberate
Document when recording starts and stops, who can view or export it, how long it is retained and how someone can raise a concern. Train staff before a camera is used on a visit.
Further reading: ICO guidance on body-worn video.
All guides
Choosing a dashcam for a Lagos bus
Start with the journey you need to understand, then choose the camera.
Choose the views
Decide whether you need road, driver or cabin views. Passenger entry and exit counting is a separate requirement: ask for a demonstration with the camera position and bus layout you will use.
Plan for power and connectivity
Check the vehicle power supply, mounting position, mobile network coverage and data costs. Ask how recordings are stored during a network interruption and how they are retrieved afterwards.
Test a complete journey
Try daytime, darkness, traffic and a crowded boarding stop. Review a clip alongside its time and location. Agree installation, storage, access and ongoing costs before ordering.

Identify the event
Connect the journey, vehicle, destination and timestamp. Keep the source of each piece of information clear so a reviewer can understand where it came from.
Keep the useful context
Link the arrival event to the relevant camera clip or handover record. A location alone cannot establish what was handed over or who accepted it.
Review and share carefully
Check the record before sharing. Limit the recipient and the information included, and agree who can authorise disclosure. Keep an example clearly labelled when demonstrating the workflow.
All guides
Clear questions. Responsible visibility.
Location and camera records can be sensitive. Agree who can see them, why they are needed and when they should be deleted before using them.
Plan access around people
Define the people who can access live views, review recordings and share records. For family location sharing, make participation and permissions clear to everyone involved.
Ask for a written security specification

Request details of encryption in transit and storage, account access controls, access logs, hosting country, subprocessors, recording retention and deletion. These details must be confirmed for your future setup; this website does not claim a certification or a specific hosting location.
Agree retention and deletion
Choose a retention period for each kind of record and document how deletion requests and incident holds are handled. Do this before connecting cameras or sharing personal locations.
UK and Nigeria operations
Discuss the applicable privacy obligations with your organisation’s adviser before deployment. The contact form is for general enquiries; do not upload recordings or sensitive incident details.

About this website

LensFleet Limited provides this marketing website to explain its tracking, camera and journey-record services. Contact info@lensfleet.com or write to the registered office shown in the footer. These draft website terms are not a subscription or service agreement.
Enquiries and quotations

Submitting a form asks the team to contact you. It does not create an account, confirm an order or reserve a price. Device models, installation, subscriptions, connectivity, recording storage and support must be set out in a separate written proposal.
Demonstrations and examples

Example journey records and product illustrations explain workflows. They do not represent a customer case study, actual incident or verified pilot result. Home launch interest can be registered through the waitlist enquiry form.
Use of the website

Send accurate enquiry details and do not submit private recordings or sensitive incident information through this form. Recording, tracking people and sharing evidence require a separate assessment and agreed permissions for the intended use.
Service agreement — awaiting approval

The owner must approve the contracting entity’s exact registered name, account terms, fees, cancellation, service commitments, warranties, liability provisions, applicable law and dispute process before these terms can be adopted. Product contracts and privacy terms must be supplied before customer onboarding. LensFleet is in development; this website does not accept product orders.
